newsitem.title: JAPAN: Problems at big Japanese banks over for now--BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Problems at big Japanese banks over for now--BOJ.

text.p: The problems at big Japanese banks are over for now as major financial institutions such as Nippon Credit Bank Ltd have forged ahead with restructuring plans, a senior official at the Bank of Japan told Reuters on Tuesday.
The official, in charge of the BOJ section which deals with financial problems, was also referring to a merger plan announced last week by Hokkaido Bank Ltd and Hokkaido Takushoku Bank Ltd.
"You can now take it that problems at big financial institutions such as NCB are over," the official said.
NCB, one of the nation's major banks, announced last week that it would restructure, halt overseas operations, sell off its Tokyo headquarters and post losses to dispose of problem loans.
The BOJ and the Finance Ministry also announced that they would extend full support to the restructuring plan.
"We supported the plan not because it is a big bank but because we thought NCB can restructure itself as the bank's liabilities did not exceed its assets," he said.
"It is important for us not to let woes at Japanese financial institutions cause problems overseas," he said.
